subject.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration

question: For legacy BLOB/TEXT primary-key values that collide after normalization, should OpenClaw keep the migration fail-closed with operator cleanup, or must `openclaw doctor --fix` provide a supported non-destructive recovery before this ships?
rationale: The patch correctly avoids silent data loss, but choosing between operator intervention and a productized collision-recovery workflow is a durable persisted-state and upgrade-policy decision.

options.title: Keep fail-closed recovery
options.body: Retain the collision error and ensure its guidance accurately describes a supported backup and manual-resolution path.

options.title: Add doctor remediation
options.body: Design a non-destructive doctor workflow that identifies conflicting durable rows and requires an explicit operator choice before rewriting them.

options.title: Pause collision-path change
options.body: Defer this migration enhancement until maintainers choose the permanent collision-recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed recovery
recommendation.body: Retain the collision error and ensure its guidance accurately describes a supported backup and manual-resolution path.

likelyOwner.reason: The underlying STRICT migration originated in the SQLite safety-hardening work.
